Rashi on Bava Metzia 7b:11:1.hebrew: צררי אתפסה - מעות צרורות או כספים מסר לה ליחוד כתובתה, כשנשאה או לאחר מכאן, שלא יטריחוה יורשים אם תתאלמן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 7b:11:1.english: He gave her bundles - Bundled coins or money he handed over to her specifically for her marriage contract, either when he married her or thereafter, so that the heirs would not trouble her if she becomes a widow.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 7b:12:1.hebrew: לעולם איפוך קמייתא - ודקשיא לך דרבנן אדרבנן, לא תיקשי: דטעמייהו דרבנן בכתובה לאו משום דחיישינן לפירעון, דמאן דפרע ואהדר ליה שטרא — לאלתר קרע ליה, אלא משום דחיישינן לשתי כתובות — שמא חזר וכתב לה כתובה אחרת שניה לאחר שנפלה זאת מידה. ו"אין הבעל מודה" דקתני — לאו באומר "פרעתי", אלא באומר: "אל תחזרו לה, שיש בידה אחרת, ותוציא על יורשי שטר אחר שטר":
Rashi on Bava Metzia 7b:12:1.english: Actually, reverse the first baraita - And that which was difficult to you regarding the contradiction of the Rabbis against the Rabbis, do not let it be difficult: for the reason of the Rabbis in the case of a ketubah is not because we suspect repayment, for one who repays and the document is returned to him tears it immediately; rather, it is because we suspect that there were two ketubot, lest he went back and wrote for her another, second ketubah after this one fell from her hand. And that which is taught, "and the husband does not admit," is not referring to a case where he says, "I repaid it," but where he says: "Do not return it to her, for she has another in her possession, and she will produce document after document against my heirs."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 7b:13:1.hebrew: מחלוקת - האי "יחלוקו" דקאמר ר"ש [ב"ג], דמשמע חולקין בשוה — כך שמעתי משום ר' יצחק ב"ר מנחם, ונראה בעיני:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 7b:13:1.english: Dispute - This refers to this ruling of "they shall divide" that Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said, which implies that they divide equally; so I heard in the name of Rabbi Yitzchak, son of Rabbi Menachem, and it appears correct in my eyes.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 7b:13:2.hebrew: ושניהם אדוקים בתורף - כלומר, או שניהם אדוקין בתורף. ותורף — גילוי של שטר: מקום הלוה והמלוה והמעות והזמן. טופס — שאר כל לשון השטר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 7b:13:2.english: And both are grasping the essential part - That is to say: Or both are grasping the essential part. And the essential part [toref] is the disclosure of the document: the place of the borrower and the lender, the money, and the date. The standard part [tofes] is all the rest of the text of the document.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 7b:13:3.hebrew: זה נוטל כו' - דמאי דתפיס דידיה הוא, כדקתני לעיל: ”זה נוטל עד מקום שידו מגעת כו'“. ולקמן מפרש למאי מיבעי ליה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 7b:13:3.english: This one takes etc. - For what he is grasping is his, as it teaches earlier: “This one takes until the place where his hand reaches, etc.” And later, the Gemara explains what he needs it for:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 7b:1:1.english: What is different about falling into the hand of a judge - From falling into the hand of another person:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 7b:1:2.english: This is what it is saying: And another - One who is neither the borrower nor the lender.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 7b:1:3.hebrew: שמצא שטר שנפל - כבר ליד הדיין. ומאי ניהו הך נפילה? דכתיב ביה הנפק:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 7b:1:3.english: Who found a note that had fallen - [That it had] already [come] into the hand of the judge. And what is this "falling"? That a ratification [henpek] was written on it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 7b:1:4.hebrew: לא יוציאוהו מידו - לא לוה ולא מלוה, עד שיבא אליהו, או עדים שראו מיד מי נפל:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 7b:1:4.english: They may not remove it from his hand - Neither the debtor nor the creditor [may remove it], until Elijah comes, or [until] witnesses [come] who saw from whose hand it fell.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 7b:2:1.english: For repayment - Perhaps the debtor is telling the truth in claiming that he repaid it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 7b:3:1.hebrew: ורבי יוסי לא חייש לפירעון - דמאן דמהדרי ליה שטר פרוע, לאלתר זהיר ביה לקורעו, ולא משהי ליה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 7b:3:1.english: And Rabbi Yosei does not suspect repayment - For one to whom a repaid [promissory] note is returned is immediately careful to tear it up, and does not keep it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 7b:4:1.english: When the husband admits - That he has not paid her her marriage contract.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 7b:4:2.hebrew: אין הבעל מודה - שאמר: פרעתי, ומידי נפל:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 7b:4:2.english: The husband does not admit - That he said: “I paid [it], and it fell from my hand.”

Rashi on Bava Metzia 7b:5:1.english: [While] she is still under her husband - That he has not divorced her.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 7b:5:2.english: He must return it to the wife - For a person is not accustomed to pay a marriage contract before divorce.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 7b:12:1.hebrew: דחיישינן לשתי כתובות - ובלאו איפוך לא מצי לאוקמא דרבי יוסי חייש לשתי כתובות; דא"כ, עודה תחת בעלה — אמאי יחזיר לאשה כשאין הבעל מודה:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 7b:12:1.english: That we suspect two marriage contracts - And without reversing [the first baraita], one could not establish that Rabbi Yosei suspects two marriage contracts; for if so, while she is still under her husband, why would [the finder] return [it] to the woman when the husband does not admit?

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 7b:13:1.hebrew: מחלוקת - פרש"י דהיינו "יחלוקו" דקאמר רשב"ג. והדין עמו שלא רצה לפרש פלוגתא דרבי ורשב"ג, משום דהיכי קאמר: "אבל אחד אדוק בטופס כו'" — משמע דהתם לא פליגי; וזה אינו, דגם שם, אם אינו מקוים, לא שקיל לרבי מידי:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 7b:13:1.english: A dispute - Rashi explained that this refers to [the ruling of] "they shall divide" that Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel stated. And he is justified in not wishing to interpret [it as] the dispute between Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, because since it says: "But [if] one is grasping the standard part, etc.," it implies that there they do not disagree; and this is not so, for there too, if [the promissory note] is not ratified, according to Rabbi [the creditor] takes nothing at all.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 7b:1:1.hebrew: מאי שנא ליד דיין - לספרים דגרסי בשנויא "והיכי דמי כגון דכתוב ביה הנפק", השתא לא ידע ד"נפל ליד דיין" דהיינו הנפק, אלא סבור דהיינו שהדיין מצאו, ולכך בעי: מאי שנא דיין מאיש אחר? ולספרים דלא גרסי בתר הכי "והיכי דמי כגון דכתוב ביה הנפק", ידע שפיר השתא ד"נפל ליד דיין" היינו שכתוב בו הנפק, ומיבעיא ליה: מאי שנא כתוב בו הנפק דלא יוציאו לעולם? הלא אם אין כתוב בו הנפק, נראה דכ"ש הוא שלא יוציאו עולמית, דאיכא למימר: שמא כתב ללות ולא לוה; ומשני: ד"לא מיבעיא" קאמר:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 7b:1:1.english: What is different about [a note that fell] into the possession of a judge - According to texts that read in the resolution: "And what are the circumstances? For example, where a ratification was written in it" — at this point [the Gemara] did not know that "it fell into the possession of a judge" means a ratification; rather, it assumed that it means that the judge found it, and therefore it asks: What is different about a judge than another person? And according to texts that do not read after this: "And what are the circumstances? For example, where a ratification was written in it" — [the Gemara] already knew well at this point that "it fell into the possession of a judge" means that a ratification was written in it, and it was inquiring: What is different about [a case where] a ratification was written in it, that he may never produce it? After all, if a ratification is not written in it, it seems all the more so that he should never produce it, as it can be said: "Perhaps he wrote [the document intending] to borrow, but did not borrow"! And [the Gemara] answers that [the baraita] is speaking [in the format of] "it is not necessary [to state]".

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 7b:4:1.hebrew: בזמן שהבעל מודה יחזיר לאשה - דלא חיישינן לקנוניא. וליכא למיחש לשמא כתב בניסן ולא נשא עד תשרי, דמנה ומאתים משתעבדי מן האירוסין אף בלא כתובה, דאירוסין קלא אית להו; ולקודם אירוסין ליכא למיחש דכתב לה. ותוספת נמי: לאביי דאמר "עדיו בחתומיו זכין לו" — א"ש, ור' אסי יעמיד כשהקנה לה:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 7b:4:1.english: When the husband admits, he must return it to the wife - For we are not concerned about collusion. And there is no concern lest he wrote the marriage contract in Nisan and did not marry her until Tishrei, for the statutory sum of one hundred and two hundred zuz becomes liened from the time of betrothal even without a marriage contract, since betrothal generates publicity; and concerning prior to betrothal, there is no concern that he wrote it for her. And regarding the additional amount as well: according to Abaye, who said: "Its witnesses, by their signatures, acquire for him," it works out well; and Rabbi Assi will establish the baraita as referring to a case where he transferred it to her.
